question: What semi-supervised learning is applied?

evidence: Our semi-supervised approach is quite straightforward: first a model is trained on the training set and then this model is used to predict the labels of the silver data. This silver data is then simply added to our training set, after which the model is retrained. However, an extra step is applied to ensure that the silver data is of reasonable quality. Instead of training a single model initially, ten different models were trained which predict the labels of the silver instances. If the highest and lowest prediction do not differ more than a certain threshold the silver instance is maintained, otherwise it is discarded.

title: UG18 at SemEval-2018 Task 1: Generating Additional Training Data for Predicting Emotion Intensity in Spanish
answer_short: The semi-supervised learning method applied is training a model on the training set, using it to predict labels for silver data, adding the silver data to the training set, and retraining the model, with a quality filter based on model predictions.
answer_rationale: The semi-supervised learning method described in the document involves training a model on the initial training set, using it to predict labels for unlabeled silver data, adding the silver data to the training set, and retraining the model. An additional quality filter is applied: if the highest and lowest predictions for a silver instance do not differ by more than a threshold, the instance is kept; otherwise, it is discarded. This method is applied to both LSTM and feed-forward networks and is only applicable to EI tasks.
